title: Mass production of human airway-like neutrophils via transmigration in an organotypic model of human airways
protocol: Seed H441 cells on an Alvetex scaffold to achieve ALI as observed in the lung.
Remove outermost tabs of plastic from scaffolds carefully without cracking them.
Add 70% ethanol dropwise to filters to rehydrate them and allow for coating with rat tail collagen Type I.
Grow H441 cells in T-75 flasks or equivalent using DMEM-F12 + 10% FBS at 37°C + 5% CO2.
Passage H441 cells at least twice before use in the model.
Discard H441 cells after passage 21.
Do not allow H441 cells to grow more than 90% confluent.
Split H441 cells every 2-3 days.
Leave collagen at 25°C for ∼20 min before use.
Remove Alvetex inserts from package.
Snap off outermost tab of Alvetex insert carefully.
Add 2–3 drops of 70% sterile filtered ethanol to Alvetex membrane.
Dry the filter until slightly opaque.
Coat Alvetex membranes with 200 μL Rat Tail Collagen I at 3 mg/mL.
Spread collagen evenly over filter without touching it.
Store coated Alvetex membranes at 37°C + 5% CO2 for 3-24 hours.
Incubate the 90% confluent T-75 flask containing H441 cells with 2 mL trypsin at 37°C + 5% CO2 for 5 minutes or until cells completely detach from the flask.
Neutralize trypsin by adding 8 mL of DMEM-F12 + 10% FBS to the flask.
Transfer the trypsinized H441 cells into a 15 mL conical tube, remove a 10 μL aliquot for cell count.
Centrifuge the conical tube at 800 × g for 10 minutes to pellet the H441 cells.
Mix the 10 μL aliquot of cells with 10 μL of EB/AO live/dead stain.
Quantify the number of cells using a hemacytometer or similar cell-counting method.
Calculate the total number of cells in the pellet using the formula: (#cells counted) * 2 * 10^4 * 10 = total cells.
Discard the supernatant after centrifuging the cells.
Resuspend the cells in DMEM-F12 + 10% FBS to achieve a final concentration of 2.5 ∗ 10^5 cells/mL.
Add 1.5 mL of DMEM-F12 + 10% FBS to the bottom of the well.
Rinse the bottom of the filter with additional DMEM-F12 + 10% FBS or RPMI if the media turns yellow due to residual collagen.
Gently add 1 mL of resuspended H441 cells (2.5 ∗ 10^5 cells/mL) apically on top of the filter.
Grow the cells at 37°C + 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Aspirate all media from both the basal and apical sides the next day.
Replace with 1.5 mL of AIM + USG basally (bottom of the filter).
Leave the apical side exposed to air.
Aspirate the media from the opening between the wall of the well and the filter without removing the filter.
Use freshly prepared AIM + USG for each media change.
Avoid bubbles under the filter during media changes.
Transfer filters to a clean 12-well plate on Day 3 or 4 after seeding.
Flip the filters and use them on Day 14 from the seeding date.
Do not use the plate later than Day 19 from the seeding date.
Collect blood in an EDTA tube (final concentration 1.5–2.0 mM) in the clinic or appropriate location for phlebotomy.
Add 6 mL of Polymorphprep™ (PMP) to a 15 mL conical tube.
Slowly layer 6 mL of whole blood on top of the PMP solution.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 42 min at room temperature with slow acceleration and minimal brake.
Remove the plasma and top mononuclear cell band (upper band).
Separate components 1 & 2.
Flip the filter if attached to component 1 according to Method video S1.
Flip the filter if attached to component 2 according to Method video S2.
Piece the components back together.
Place the filter into a 12-well plate containing transmigration media such as CFASN or LTB4.
Tile the plate to avoid introducing air bubbles.
Collect the neutrophil band using a Pasteur pipette.
Transfer the collected neutrophil band to a clean conical tube.
Note donors with excessive red blood cell contamination alongside the neutrophils.
Add one volume of 0.45% w/v NaCl to the neutrophils.
Gently mix by inverting the tube 3–4 times.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5–10 min.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Keep neutrophils on ice at all times from this step forward.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of ice-cold, sterile cell-culture water.
Incubate on ice for 30 s.
Add 5 mL of ice-cold 1.8% NaCl to restore osmolarity.
Gently mix by inverting the tube 3–4 times.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Repeat red blood cell lysis until no red cells are visible, up to a total of 2–3 times.
Resuspend the neutrophils in cold RPMI at a concentration of 1×10^7 cells/1 mL and keep on ice until needed.
Reverse the orientation of H441 epithelial cells grown at ALI on Alvetex filters.
Prepare transmigration media immediately after neutrophils are purified.
Add purified blood neutrophils on top of the basal aspect of the epithelium.
Allow neutrophils to transmigrate towards the fluid bathing the apical aspect of the epithelium.
Dilute CFASN 1:3 with RPMI for a 12-well plate.
Aliquot 2 ml of diluted CFASN into each well of a non-tissue culture treated plate.
Separate components 1 and 2.
Place both components upside down in the sterile packaging from the new plate for the transmigration assay.
Using forceps, gently nudge the filter and pick up the opposite end.
Invert the component and place it back on the center of the bottom side of component 1.
Align the clips of component 2 with the tabs on component 1.
Gently press component 2 back onto component 1 to ensure all clips click into place.
Revert the reconstructed filter apparatus and place it into the appropriate well containing the transmigration fluid.
Slightly tilt the plate when adding the filter to avoid introducing air bubbles.
Use forceps to pick up the filter by aligning the curve of the forceps with the curve of the membrane.
Place the membrane back down in the center of the bottom side of component 1 without inversion if removal is difficult.
Align the clips of component 2 with the tabs on component 1 and gently press component 2 onto component 1 so that all clips click into place.
Take care not to touch the filter when pressing components together.
Slightly tilt the plate when adding the filter to the well to avoid air bubbles.
Add 100 μl of purified blood neutrophils (1*10^7 cells/1 ml) to the top of the filter.
Take care not to touch the filter or pierce it with the pipette tip.
Ensure that the plate is flat and neutrophils are evenly dispersed across the filter.
Move the plate gently into the incubator at 37°C + 5% CO2.
Allow transmigration for a desired amount of time, typically 4 hours for early emigrated neutrophils or 10-18 hours overnight for late-stage phenotypes.
Remove the filters after transmigration is complete.
Release epithelial cells and non-transmigrating neutrophils from Alvetex filter using Accutase.
Gently pipette up and down twice with a P1000 to resuspend transmigrated neutrophils and transfer to a 2 mL tube.
Spin cells at 800 × g for 5 min at room temperature to pellet.
Discard or save the supernatant for other assays.
Wash the pellet by adding 1 ml of 1× PBS + 2.5 mM EDTA and spinning at 800 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant after washing.
Resuspend neutrophils in 250 μL RPMI.
Make a 10 μL aliquot for counting cells using a hemacytometer.
Adjust the concentration of neutrophils to 1.2 × 10^5 cells/120 μL for the bacteria-killing assay.
Inoculate P. aeruginosa (PA01) in 3 mL of LB media the day before transmigration.
Grow overnight at 37°C at 200 rpm.
Prepare a mock-inoculated tube to check for contamination in the LB media.
Subculture bacteria by pipetting 10 μL of overnight growth into 3 mL of fresh LB media.
Grow at 37°C with shaking until OD600 = 0.4–0.6.
Generate a standard curve to convert OD600 to colony forming units (CFU).
Mix bacteria and neutrophils together.
Rotate the mixture end over end to prevent settling of cells during the assay.
Place the rotator in a 37°C + 5% CO2 incubator.
Grow PA01 at 30°C if mucoid colonies with poorly defined edges are formed.
Transmigrate neutrophils towards LTB4, a control chemoattractant.
Compare bacteria-killing capacity of neutrophils transmigrated towards LTB4 and those transmigrated towards CFASN using Mann-Whitney U test.
Centrifuge bacteria at 16,000 × g for 2 minutes at 25°C.
Resuspend the bacteria pellet in 500 μL of warm RPMI + 10% FBS.
Incubate at 37°C + 5% CO2 on a rotator end-over-end for 30 minutes.
Dilute 15 μL of bacteria in 3 mL of RPMI + 10% FBS warmed to 37°C (1.2 × 10^5 CFU/60 μL).
Add 60 μL of bacteria to 120 μL of neutrophils for a multiplicity of infection of 1.
Prepare a control tube containing only bacteria without neutrophils by adding 60 μL of bacteria to 120 μL of RPMI.
Rotate all tubes end-over-end at 37°C + 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Pipette 10 μL of 1% w/v Triton X-100 into Row A of a prepared 96-well plate.
Pipette 180 μL of 1× PBS into rows B through G.
Label LB agar plates.
Pipette 90 μL from the bacteria-killing reaction into a well of row A.
Pipette up and down to mix and lyse the neutrophils to release intracellular bacteria.
Spin the cells at 100 × g for 7 min to pellet the neutrophils, but not the bacteria (optional).
Incubate the pelleted neutrophils in 100 μL of Accutase at 37°C + 5% CO2 for 5 min (optional).
Neutralize by adding 400 μL of DMEM + 10% FBS.
Spin at 100 × g for 7 min to pellet the neutrophils, but not the bacteria.
Transfer 20 μL of sample from Row A into Row B using a multichannel pipette.
Mix up and down to evenly distribute the bacteria.
Repeat 10× serial dilutions.
Spot 5 μL of each dilution onto an LB plate.
Mix 5–6 replicates of 6 dilutions on a single 10 cm LB plate.
Allow spots to dry by leaving plates exposed to air for 10 minutes, ensuring the lid is off but the plates are covered or in a sterile hood.
Dry plates further in an oven if necessary to minimize spreading.
Place the lid back onto the plates.
Incubate plates inverted at 30°C for 12–16 hours.
Count and record the number of colony-forming units (CFUs) in each spot when colonies are easily observable but not overgrown.
